messages:
eli: handing off. I'm primary for the next 8h. Ongoing incident: model-serving nodes in us-west-2 experiencing intermittent OOMs on high-seq requests, causing failovers to small-model variant and elevated tail latency. pagerduty-bot alerted at 1768502500.

maria: noted. what's the current customer impact? any SLOs breached?

eli: currently affecting ~6% of traffic to text-gen endpoints for customers pinned to the large-32k model. Observed 95p token latency spikes ~3-5s higher, and some requests are getting the fallback model response (shorter completions). No 5xx increase systemwide, mainly graceful fallback.

samir: infra notes: a subset of GPU hosts (g4-pw-09*) have kernel OOMs when sequence length > 16k and batch size > 16. We repro'd locally with stress script. Crash loop started after yesterday's kernel patch + new CUDA driver.

eli: mitigation in progress: temporarily draining the 4 affected hosts, switching traffic to reserve pool, and enabling model-variant hard routing for enterprise customers where correctness trumps latency.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-451 created. Priority: P2. Playbook: "model-serving-oom". Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving-oom

jess: can you paste the commands used to drain + node check? putting into the runbook.

samir: drain command we ran:```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-09 && kubectl drain gpu-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# verify pods rescheduled
kubectl get pods -o wide | grep model-server | grep gpu-09
```
We also toggled ephemeral autoscale:```json
{"scale_target": "reserve-pool", "min": 2, "max": 8}
```

maria: monitoring: added a temporary alert for "model_oom_count > 0 on any host" and increased the retention for request traces for the affected model tag. Also enabled KV-cache bypass for requests that previously hit the corrupted host to avoid cache lookup errors.

eli: handoff checklist for whoever takes over: 1) keep affected hosts drained until kernel rollback/driver fix deployed; 2) ensure reserve pool capacity >= current baseload; 3) update customers flagged as impacted (see incident table); 4) coordinate with infra for driver rollback window; 5) watch for regressions in fallback rate.

maria: gaps: we don't have an automated rollback job for the problematic driver. manual rollback steps are in infra runbook but needs signoff from security for older driver binaries. samir you and I should coordinate windows and notify compliance.

samir: yep. I'll prepare a canary rollback to one host this afternoon (ETA 2h). If canary looks good (no OOM in 30m under load), we'll schedule a rolling rollback during off-peak with a 10m pause between hosts.

eli: who is secondary for the next 8h? @maria please?

maria: I can be secondary for first 4h, then @jess will take the following 4h. Jess, you good?

jess: I can cover. I'll be reachable by phone. Also adding a quick customer message draft for CS: "We're investigating elevated tail latency and temporary fallbacks for some large-context requests in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress; no data loss. We'll update within 2 hours." Any edits?

eli: looks good. add link to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-451 and note affected model tag: large-32k-v2.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty: eskalation policy active. Primary: eli (oncall), Secondary: maria (sre).

maria: runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving-oom (main), https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-drivers (infra), and https://redwood.internal/playbooks/notify-customers (comm).

eli: open action items before handoff complete: [A1] Confirm reserve pool autoscale set and healthy (samir). [A2] Publish customer notice (jess). [A3] Kick off driver canary rollback + smoke test (samir + maria). [A4] Keep traces and logs attached to the incident ticket (eli).

samir: A1 done (reserve pool scaled to 6), A3 started (canary scheduled), will post results to this thread.

jess: A2 drafted and sent to CS for review (sent to #customer-comm).

eli: last note — if you take over, watch the fallback_rate metric and the rate of "model_variant_override" traces. If both go above 8% for >10m, escalate to P1 and bring product oncall.

maria: I will be in the channel for first 4h and will notify when I hand off to jess. Good luck and thanks. :thumbsup: 

eli: thanks team. Handoff complete. I'm signing off at 15:40 UTC.

samir: canary looks healthy at +35m under 2x synthetic load, no OOMs so far. will proceed with rolling window at 16:30 UTC unless someone objects.

jess: acknowledged, taking secondary. will monitor the thread and own customer comms.

oncall-bot: Note: attach logs using: /incident attach INC-2026-451 /var/logs/model-server/gpu-09.log

eli: thread closed for handoff; please reopen if anything regresses.
